items.prompt: In a contiguous buffer of n values, what is the typical cost of reading index i?
items.whyRight: Address is base plus i times width, so the jump is constant time.
whyWrong: Logarithmic search assumes a sorted probe loop, not a direct index read.
Linear cost would mean walking from the start; indexing skips that walk.
n log n belongs to comparison sorts, not a single indexed read.

items.prompt: You insert one value in the middle of an array of n elements. What dominates the cost?
items.whyRight: Everything after the hole must move to keep the buffer contiguous.
whyWrong: Hashing appears in maps, not in a plain contiguous insert.
Tree rebalancing is a different structure's story.
A pointer rewrite describes a linked-list splice, not an array middle insert.

items.prompt: Repeated appends into a dynamic array that doubles when full are best described as what amortized cost per append?
items.whyRight: Most appends write one slot; occasional full copies are paid across many appends.
whyWrong: A single growth copy is O(n), but that is not the per-append amortized bound.
Logarithmic cost is not the usual dynamic-array append story.
Quadratic would require nested copying on every append, which doubling avoids.

items.prompt: Jumping to index i is the hot path. Array or linked list?
choices: Linked list — always faster for jumps
List, because cache lines do not matter
items.whyRight: An array computes the address; a list still walks i nodes.
whyWrong: A list is slower for arbitrary index jumps, not faster.
The costs differ by a linear walk versus constant addressing.
Cache behavior usually favors dense arrays; it does not flip the asymptotic walk.

items.prompt: You already hold a node pointer and must remove that node from a chain. Which structure keeps the edit local?
items.whyRight: Relinking neighbors is O(1) when the node is already in hand.
whyWrong: An array still shifts the suffix after the removed index.
A sorted set solves order queries, not this local splice question.
A hash set of values does not rewire a chain of nodes.

items.prompt: Which statement about arrays is safe to say in a phone screen?
choices: Middle insert is O(n) because the tail shifts
Every insert is O(1) including the middle
Index reads are O(n) on average
items.whyRight: Contiguity forces a shift when you open a hole in the middle.
whyWrong: Middle inserts are not constant time on a plain array.
Index reads are O(1), not average linear.
Arrays routinely store integers and many other element types.
